abstract: Maintains acoustic hydrophone telemetry records and underwater noise mitigation deployments
system_message:
You are the Subsea Environmental Acoustics Officer (ACOUS). Your responsibilities include maintaining acoustic hydrophone telemetry records, verifying underwater noise mitigation deployments, and tracking sediment plume turbidity monitoring records across candidate offshore installation contractors.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Maintains acoustic hydrophone telemetry records and underwater noise mitigation deployments（HYDRO）
information_points.content:
ACOUS-HYDRO-XM6：According to the subsea piling mitigation readiness checklist, Boreas Heavy Marine Consortium has an active subsea bubble curtain system confirmed as installed and operational. Additionally, far-field calibrated hydrophone test records at 750 meters distance from its test rig indicate an underwater pile driving acoustic exposure of 160 dB re 1 uPa across full-energy hydraulic hammer impacts.
ACOUS-HYDRO-FTT：For Nordic Wind Offshore Services, the readiness checklist confirms an active subsea bubble curtain system is installed and operational. However, calibrated hydrophone test measurements at 750 meters distance show an underwater pile driving acoustic exposure of 172 dB re 1 uPa during full-energy hydraulic hammer impacts.
ACOUS-HYDRO-BCU：Zephyr Maritime Installation Group maintains an active subsea bubble curtain system in an operational state according to its subsea piling readiness checklist. Hydrophone testing at 750 meters distance confirms an underwater pile driving acoustic exposure of 160 dB re 1 uPa across full-energy hydraulic hammer impacts.

information_points.title: Sediment plume turbidity monitoring（TURB）
information_points.content:
ACOUS-TURB-LWB：For Nordic Wind Offshore Services, sensor deployment logs along the seabed foundation perimeter during test trenching measure a baseline nephelometric turbidity of 12 NTU.
ACOUS-TURB-P02：Turbidity monitoring logs for Zephyr Maritime Installation Group document a baseline nephelometric turbidity of 25 NTU along the seabed foundation perimeter during test trenching.
ACOUS-TURB-2BU：Turbidity sensor deployment logs around the seabed foundation perimeter during test trenching record a baseline nephelometric turbidity of 18 NTU for Boreas Heavy Marine Consortium.
